Typedef Documentation

typedef struct _HxImage_t HxImage_t

HxImage_t is a data structure used for both on-screen and off-screen images. It is used by the image creation and drawing API defined in hximage.h, and the blitting functions defined in hxgraphics.h.

Unlike HxImageDescription_t, allocating a HxImage_t structure also allocates the memory for the image pixels.

This is an opaque structure.

Definition at line 53 of file hximage.h.

typedef struct _HxImageDescription_t HxImageDescription_t

_HxImageDescription_t is a structure containing fields that describe the dimensions and format of an image. HxImageDescriptionGetBounds, HxImageDescriptionGetFormat, and HxImageDescriptionGetData can be used to retrieve image information once the structure has been created.

The structure can be created in two ways.

If the source data is uncompressed raster data, the application uses HxImageDescriptionNewFromData, providing image parameters together with a pointer to the source data. The image structure is returned.

If the source data is a coming from a compressed image file, the application uses HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile, sending the filename string, including the path. The image structure is returned.

This is an opaque structure.

enum HxImageFlags_t

Enumerator:
kHxImageFlagsNone 
kHxImageFlagsLocked  Image is locked in place in system memory until deleted. This is used to allocate a surface that can be directly modified by another rendering library while being used for drawing. You still will need to call HxImageLockSurface and HxImageUnlockSurface to get a pointer, but that pointer will not change.

This surface is not stored in video memory, so graphics operations with this surface may be slower than normal.

HxResult HxImageConvertDfbFormat ( int32_t  dfbFormat,
HxPixelFormat_t *  pFormat 
)

Convert a DirectFB pixel format to a HxUI format.

HxImageConvertDfbFomat convrts a DFBSurfacePixelFormat value into the corresponding HxPixelFormat_t value. This is usually used with the output of directfb-csource to convert the fields of a DFBSurfaceDescription structure into arguments for the HxImageDescriptionNewFromData API.

To avoid contamination between the DirectFB and HxUI headers, the DFB format is passed as an integer to this function, so if you're using C++, you may need a parameter cast.

Parameters:
dfbFormat IN: DFB format value
pFormat OUT: Pointer to the display pixel format
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if the format cannot be converted.

HxResult HxImageDescriptionDraw ( HxImageDescription_t *  pDescription,
HxImage_t *  pDstImage,
const HxRectangle_t *  pSrcRect,
const HxRectangle_t *  pDstRect 
)

Draw an image description.

HxImageDescriptionDraw draws an image based on the pointer to a HxImageDescription_t structure obtained from a prior call to HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile or HxImageDescriptionNewFromData.

pDstImage can be either an on-screen window, or an off-screen canvas. If NULL, the application window is used.

The bounds of the source data is defined by pSrcRect. If pSrcRect is NULL, the entire source image is used.

The bounds into which the source data is stretched is defined by pDstRect. If pDstRect is NULL, the bounds of the main application window is used.

The source data is stretch-blitted to the destination, based on the source and destination rectangles.

If the source data has an alpha channel or if it was loaded from a file format that supports a transparent color index (or source color key), then this function sets the blitting flags for the destination image appropriately. If the application wants to set custom blit flags, then use HxImageDescriptionDrawWithFlags.

Parameters:
pDescription IN: Pointer to HxImageDescription_t
pDstImage IN: Destination image, widget, window, or NULL to use application window.
pSrcRect IN: Bounds of source data to be drawn, or NULL
pDstRect IN: Destination bounds where source drawn, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails.

HxResult HxImageDescriptionDrawWithFlags ( HxImageDescription_t *  pDescription,
HxImage_t *  pDstImage,
const HxRectangle_t *  pSrcRect,
const HxRectangle_t *  pDstRect,
HxBlitFlags_t  flags 
)

Draw an image description with blit flags.

HxImageDescriptionDrawWithFlags is a variation of HxImageDescriptionDraw, and allows the application to customize the blit flags.

This function will call HxGraphicsSetBlitFlags on the destination image using the value passed in as the flags parameter. Use kHxBlitBlendAlphaChannel to do alpha blending or use kHxBlitSrcColorKey to mask out a color from the image. If you are copying an image and want to preserve the alpha channel, use kHxBlitNoFX.

See hxuitypes.h for a full listing of HxBlitFlags and their descriptions.

Parameters:
pDescription IN: Pointer to HxImageDescription_t
pDstImage IN: Destination image, widget, window, or NULL to use application window.
pSrcRect IN: Bounds of source data to be drawn, or NULL
pDstRect IN: Destination bounds where source drawn, or NULL
flags IN: Blitting flags (see hxuitypes.h)
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails.

HxResult HxImageDescriptionNewFromData ( int32_t  width,
int32_t  height,
HxPixelFormat_t  format,
int32_t  rowBytes,
const void *  pData,
HxImageDescription_t **  hDescription 
)

Create an image description from a data pointer.

HxImageDescriptionNewFromData creates an image description structure from the arguments. This API is a variation of HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile, with a pointer to the image data passed as one of the arguments. The image data must be uncompressed raster data.

The image can be subsequently drawn by calling HxImageDraw.

The image structure must be deleted after its use by calling HxImageDescriptionDelete.

Parameters:
width IN: Pixel width of the image
height IN: Pixel height of the image
format IN: Pixel format of the image data
rowBytes IN: Bytes per row of the image
pData IN: Pointer to the uncompressed raster data
hDescription OUT: A handle to an image description structure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile ( const char *  pFilename,
HxImageDescription_t **  hDescription 
)

Create an image description from a graphics file.

HxImageDescriptionNewFromFile returns information about a graphics file. It uses the DirectFB IDirectFBImageProvider interface to read the image header. The format of the source data can be JPEG, GIF, PNG, or MPEG2.

This function can be used to obtain the width and height of an image before it is drawn by a call to HxImageDraw.

The image structure must be deleted after its use by calling HxImageDescriptionDelete.

Parameters:
pFilename IN: String including full path to the graphics file
hDescription OUT: A handle to an image description structure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MISSING_RESOURCE if the image provider interface cannot be created. This error can occur if an improper path to the file is passed to this function, of if the source file does not exist.

HxResult HxImageLockSurface ( HxImage_t *  pImage,
void **  hDstBuf 
)

Lock the display, and get a pointer to its data.

HxImageLockSurface is the accessor to the data pointer for the pixel buffer associated with an offscreen canvas.

In order to get the pointer to the pixel buffer, the pixel buffer must be locked down. This prevents other threads from trying to draw to the pixel buffer at the same time. While holding this lock, no other drawing can occur. Any attempt to draw will not cause an error, but the new data will be ignored and not transferred to the canvas, even when the surface is later unlocked.

Consequently, the application must be very careful when using this API. Every call to HxImageLockSurface must have a matching call to HxImageUnlockSurface. And care must be taken during the locked phase: the application should not allow the event loop to run, which could cause a screen update to get lost.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to an offscreen canvas
hDstBuf OUT: Handle to the canvas's pixel buffer
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if pImage was not properly initilialize by HxImageNew.

HxResult HxImageNewWithFlags ( int32_t  width,
int32_t  height,
HxPixelFormat_t  format,
HxImageFlags_t  flags,
HxImage_t **  hImage 
)

Create an offscreen image with image flags.

HxImageNewWithFlags allocates an offscreen image for drawing.

If format is set to kHxPixelFormatUnknown, then the format of the offscreen image is set to the display's pixel format.

The HxImage_t is filled with white. If alpha blending of this image with another surface is needed, then the application should fill the HxImage_t with a fully transparent color (alpha = 0) before drawing into the HxImage_t, and it should use a pixel format that supports an alpha channel.

Parameters:
width IN: Pixel width of the image
height IN: Pixel height of the image
format IN: Pixel format of the image
flags IN: See HxImageFlags_t definition
hImage OUT: Handle to offscreen image
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails.
